summary: Daily run 2026-10-29, window Oct 25-28 (full 4 days) vs Oct 18-24, 1% SYSTEM sample. Step 1: 40 flags with >=3 keys spiking (ran first time). Dropped as artifacts, not attacks (following the 2026-10-27 run): cdn-header-order-only-have-single-cookie (54 keys, ~6.8M/day excess; created 2026-10-24 04:30 by c.koay, ticket 140244, baseline ~0). country-timezone-mismatch (79 keys; not edited since 2023, but the EU DST end on Oct 25 steps it up on every key; noisy until US DST ends Nov 1). ja4-dict-1-challenger and its duplicate ja4-dict-1-challenger-is-supicious-not-included (15 keys; the Oct 27 step change from an upstream JA4 dictionary or client change). g-ip-connection-type-velocity-short-term-abuse-wired-1point5x/2x/3x (11/8/6 keys; rule rewritten Oct 21 by s.alapati, ~0 before). g-cdn-ends-cl-rfc-ct-before-cl-tz-mismatch-grease (spike-scan TT created Oct 19; its name entered TELLTALE_LIST from 0 inside the baseline). DI dictionary edits by m.davies on 2026-10-27 02:06-04:17 UTC (none on Oct 28-29). dict-1 1x/5x/10x/LT, dict-3 1x/4x/LT and dict-neg1 ST/LT all now carry an impossible di_dictionary_num_matched == -99 condition, so they are disabled at source (THR-405..413). dict-7, dict-15 and dict-31 were re-thresholded: '1x' became ratio >= 3, '4x' became ratio >= 6 (descriptions say 'NAME NOT CHANGED ... RATIO IS 3x/6x'), and LT became long_term_ratio >= 3. So g-di-dict-7-match-short-term-threshold-exceeded-4x (5 keys in step 1) is a definition change inside the window and is dropped, and dict-7/15 1x are not used either. Drops on dict-3 combos after Oct 27 ~09 UTC are the edit. Ensemble-managed lists rewritten several times a day, treated as definition changes: g--e-g-ja4-suspicious-verification-patterns (6 keys; now 2 hashes, was 25 on Oct 22), g--e-ja4-global-cluster-strict (4 keys; 93-hash list) and g--e-capi-anomaly-missing-capi-version (5 keys; 376-key list re-dated Oct 28; the changelog call timed out twice, so this is not confirmed). Duplicates: sus-flag-cdn-header-order-has-sec-fetch-user (= g-cdn-header-order-has-sec-fetch-user), g-cdn-header-order-has-upgrade-insecure-requests (same sessions), cdn-header-order-contains-cache-control (= pragma). Kept with a note: g-browser-api-check-hash-chrome-windows-mismatch (4 keys, small) had its Chrome version range widened 155 -> 156 on Oct 22 (routine bump; baseline not ~0). Top surviving single flags (sampled x100, window/day vs base/day): g-device-parameter-spoofing on 7 keys (Airbnb Account Lookup 33k vs 2k, theLott Login 25k vs 6k, Expedia Taap K3 14k vs 2k, Rightmove, Blizzard ROW Reg). spoofed-os-mismatch on 6 keys (Roblox Login 252k vs 6k, MS Signup, Blizzard ROW Support, Airbnb, MS Outlook). g-di-high-risk-signature-2x-LT on 6 (Amazon IDS 121k vs 2k, Highlight AI 33k vs 2k, DoorDash 24k vs 6k, AT&T Consumer Login, Grab). cdn-header-order-ends-with-content-length on 5 (Uber SMS 1.84M vs 296k, Amazon IDS 260k vs 78k, Expedia, MS Signup, BofA Beacon ATM). di-short-count-300-fp-pixel-ratio-1 on 5 (Pinterest Login 96k vs 14k, Amazon IDS 75k vs 9k, Airbnb 21k vs 0, Pinterest Reg 13k). pragma/cache-control on 5 (Amazon IDS 247k vs 23k). upcoming-Chrome sec-ch-ua on 5 (Amazon IDS 172k vs 31k). g-ip-velocity-long-term-abuse on 5 (Roblox Signup 78k vs 16k, BofA Beacon ATM 74k vs 2k). g-di-high-risk-sig-ST on 5 (Pinterest Login 32k, BofA ATM 13k). Uber SMS also shows sec-fetch-user/upgrade-insecure-requests 1.32M vs 25k, anomalous-not-brand sec-ch-ua 1.91M vs 402k, and ip-velocity LT-2x/ST-2x 609k/542k. Step 2 (16-flag vocab /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Detection-Product-Apps/72de94d1-885d-5b9c-8ba4-dfe15c3414db/scratchpad/vocab_1029.txt, arity <= 4, limit 20): 12 surviving step-1 flags plus tracked page-bio null, GREASE, rfc ct-before-cl and g-operating-system-spoofing. Left out: artifact flags (ja4-dict-1, dict-3, dict-7) and, because of the 16-flag cap, the other tracked flags (tz no-vpn, g--e tz, rta-isp, ends-te, single-click, webgl, appleos, sec-fetch-dest). Two combos reached keys_spiking >= 5 and spike_share >= 0.5, both NEW (not subsets of a tracked combo). (1) cdn-header-order-contains-pragma + client-hints-maybe-unexpected-sec-ch-ua-for-upcoming-google-chrome-version: 5 keys, sampled share 0.82. Adding GREASE gives the same share, so the pair is preferred. Exact Oct 25-28 (created / verified): Amazon IDS K2 583,888 (4.6k/5.2k on Oct 25/26, then 262k/312k on Oct 27/28; 12% verified); Adobe Sign Up 15,545 (31%); Olo Payments 11,413 (Oct 25 only, 52%); MS Identity Signup 6,336 (15%); Pinterest Login 4,467 (5%). All keys 747,785, so the exact share on spiking keys is 0.83. Amazon IDS is 78% of it. Baseline Amazon IDS ~0.2-2.5k per 12h. (2) spoofed-os-mismatch + g-page-level-biometrics-empty-or-null + client-hints-has-not-a-brand-grease: 5 keys, sampled share 0.55 (the pair without page-bio is 0.48). Exact Oct 25-28: Roblox Login 1,148,800 (3.6k/2.9k on Oct 25/26, then 168k Oct 27 and 974k Oct 28; 7.8% verified); Roblox Signup 124,287 (28%); MS Outlook 10,318 (72%); Blizzard ROW Registration >= 5,692 (~1-2% verified); MS Identity Signup >= 4,288 (~7%). All keys 2,454,578, so the exact share is 0.53. Roblox Login is 89% of it, and Amazon IDS (~110-138k/day steady) is the largest non-spiking key. Both drafts pass validate_telltale (valid, no errors) and were NOT created. They were not added to combos.json and no telltales/*.json was written, because another agent owns combos.json and the CSVs in this run. Proposed names: g-cdn-pragma-sec-ch-ua-upcoming-chrome and g-spoofed-os-mismatch-pagebio-null-grease. Other combos with >= 5 keys had share < 0.5: pragma + GREASE 8 keys 0.16; upcoming-Chrome + GREASE 7 keys 0.37; spoofed-os + GREASE 0.48; dp-spoof + hrsig-ST + rfc ct-before-cl 0.44; dp-spoof + page-bio + rfc ct-before-cl 0.40; di-short-300 + GREASE 0.21; dp-spoof + hrsig-ST 0.11. Not re-checked this run: tracked combos that include ja4-dict-1/dict-3/dict-7 (outside the vocab).
